Title: Getting Started
Description: Welcome to your ClassFabric journey from the ground up.

Content.Title: Welcome to ClassFabric
Content.Content: Would you like a quick walkthrough of ClassFabric?
You can learn how to use ClassFabric at any time via Tutorials... in the app main menu.
You can learn how to use ClassFabric at any time via Tutorials... in the app main menu.

Content.Title: Skip tutorial
Content.Content: Click this button to skip the tutorial. Once skipped, the tutorial is marked as completed and will not show up automatically again. You can replay it anytime via Tutorials... in the main menu.

Content.Title: This is the main window
Content.Content: ClassFabric displays your class plans and other information here.

Content.Title: The main window won't block what's behind it
Content.Content: You can click through the main window to interact with content behind it. Give it a try!

Content.Title: Fade on pointer hover
Content.Content: The main window fades out when you hover over it with the mouse or tap it on a touch screen.

Content.Title: Notifications
Content.Content: When an important moment approaches, such as the time to head to class, the app raises a notification like this one. We will cover notifications in more detail later.
Now that you have met the main window, let's take a quick look at what the app can do.

Content.Title: Main menu
Content.Content: The main menu is your entry point to the app's features — everything can be reached from here.
👉 Now, click the ClassFabric icon in the system tray as shown to open the app main menu, then click Settings... to open the app settings.

Content.Title: App settings
Content.Content: This is the app settings window. You can adjust every app setting here except class plan arrangements.
Next, let's walk through a few basic settings.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableSettingsEditing"]() == true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.welcome/settings.reject")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Title: Semester start date
Content.Content: This date is the first day of the semester. It is used to compute alternating weeks for class plans: the week containing this date counts as week 1.
👉 Now, adjust the semester start date as needed
For other settings, an explanation is shown below each settings card. Refer to these explanations to understand what each setting does.

Content.Title: More options
Content.Content: This is More options.... Click it to expand entries such as Export diagnostic data, Logs... and Management.

Content.Title: Adjust other settings
Content.Content: You can also click these navigation items to switch to other settings pages and adjust more options. We will cover these pages in detail later.
Now that you have seen the app settings, let's move on to main window editing.
👉 Now, open the main menu, then click Edit main window... to enter edit mode.
However, settings editing has been disabled by management policy, so we cannot cover the settings for now.
👉 Now, open the main menu, then click Edit main window... to enter edit mode.

Content.Title: Edit mode
Content.Content: This is the main window editor, where you edit what appears on the main window.
We will cover edit mode in detail later. Next, let's look at class plan editing.
👉 Now, click Done to exit edit mode.
👉 Open the main menu, then click Edit profile... to open the profile editor.

Content.Title: Profile editing
Content.Content: This is the profile editing window — the place to edit and manage class arrangements.
This screen may look a bit overwhelming, but don't worry — we will walk through it step by step.

Content.Title: Tabs
Content.Content: These tabs switch between the different areas of the profile editor.

Content.Title: Info bar
Content.Content: Here you can see the currently active class plan and other info, and perform actions such as Save.

Tutorials.Title: Class Plan Editing: The Basics
Tutorials.Description: A first look at editing class plans.

Content.Content: Let's start with the basic concepts of the class plan system.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileEditing"]() == true) then
		service.StopTutorial()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Title: Class plan
Content.Content: Just like a timetable in real life, each class plan in ClassFabric stores the lessons for one day and automatically shows them on the main window when its activation rule is satisfied.

Content.Title: Time layout
Content.Content: Displaying a day's lessons requires not only the list of lessons but also how the day is timed. Like a daily schedule sheet in real life, a time layout stores the timing of the day for class plans to use.

Content.Title: How class plans and time layouts relate
Content.Content: As shown here, multiple class plans can share one time layout — just as one real-life daily schedule applies to many days.

Content.Title: Subject
Content.Content: Just like subjects in real life, a subject here describes the subject of a lesson in a class plan. The app comes with several built-in subjects, and you can add your own as needed.
With the basics covered, let's build your first class plan from scratch.
Before creating a class plan, we need a time layout that tells the app how your day is timed.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileEditing"]() == true or context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileTimeLayoutEditing"]() == true) then
		service.StopTutorial()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Title: Create a time layout
Content.Content: 👉 Now, click the Add button to create a time layout.

On this page you can give the time layout an easy-to-remember name.
After editing its basic info, click any blank area to close the drawer.

Content.Title: Time points
Content.Content: A time layout consists of time points; each time point represents a segment of the day.

Content.Title: Time point types
Content.Content: Time points come in two main types: Class and Break. A Class time point corresponds to one lesson in the associated class plan.

Content.Title: Create a class time point
Content.Content: 👉 Now, click the Class button to create a class time point.

We have created a class time point, and it has appeared in the editing view.
Class time points map to lessons in the class plan.

Content.Title: Edit a time point
Content.Content: 👉 Now, following your actual daily schedule, try dragging this time point, or drag its top or bottom handle to adjust its start time.

Content.Title: Edit a time point
Content.Content: You can also fine-tune a time point's details here.
Similarly, we can add a break time point the same way as above.
👉 Now, click the Break button to create a break time point.

We have created a break time point just like we did for the class time point.
Unlike class time points, break time points have no place in the class plan and are hidden on the main window by default.

Content.Title: Keep adding time points...
Content.Content: Next, following the same steps, lay out the whole day to match your actual schedule.
If several of your time layouts are similar, click Duplicate to copy the selected time layout and modify from there.
Once your time layout is done, switch to the Class plans tab to start arranging class plans.
Next, let's see how to create a class plan.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileEditing"]() == true or
		context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileClassPlanEditing"]() == true) then
		service.StopTutorial()
		return false
	end

	if (context["classfabric.sdg.profileSettingsWindow.classPlans.isCurrentWeekFull"] == true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.profileEditing/reject.multiweek-classplans.full")
		return false
	end
	
	return true
end

Content.Title: The grid class plan editor
Content.Content: This is the grid editor for class plans, where you can see the week's plans at a glance.
👉 Now, click the New class plan button under the day you want (e.g. Monday) to create a class plan.
👉 In Time layout, pick the time layout you just created; ignore the other options for now and click Create to make the class plan.
🎉 Congratulations! You have just created your first class plan.
As you can see, the new class plan shows up here. In the grid editor, each column represents a class plan active on that day.

Each row corresponds to a time point, with the matching time point of the selected plan shown at the start of the row. Every cell in the row is one lesson of the corresponding class plan at that time point.
👉 Now, double-click the cell marked (empty) to edit that lesson's subject.
👉 Pick the subject you want in the popup to finish setting the subject.

Content.Title: Quick subject entry
Content.Content: Besides double-clicking lessons to change subjects one by one, you can use the quick subject entry here to fill in the plan's subjects fast.
Just click a subject to apply it to the selected lesson, which then advances to the next lesson automatically. Give it a try.
👉 Now, enter the subjects for this class plan following your own timetable.
Next, let's look at activation rules and multi-week rotation.
Content.Script:
function onLeftButtonClicked()
	service.SkipTutorial()
	return true
end

function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileEditing"]() == true or
		context["classfabric.management.policy.getDisableProfileClassPlanEditing"]() == true) then
		service.StopTutorial()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Title: Activation rules
Content.Content: As the name suggests, an activation rule defines when a class plan is active — for example, on odd-numbered Mondays.

Content.Title: Multi-week rotation
Content.Content: In ClassFabric, a class plan can use multi-week rotation in its activation rule — for example, active only in odd weeks, or in the first week of every three weeks.
Multi-week rotation is calculated from the Semester Start Date in settings: the start date and the seven days that follow it (that day included) count as the first week of the semester.
👉 Now, click the Class plan info... button to open a plan's details.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.sdg.profileSettingsWindow.classPlans.isEmpty"] == true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.profileEditing/reject.multiweek-classplans.empty")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: This is where a plan's activation rule is adjusted. The same screen appears when creating a class plan from the grid editor, letting you set its activation rule before creating it.
Here you choose which weekday the plan is active on. When creating via the grid editor, this is filled in automatically.
Here you choose in which weeks the plan is active.
👉 Now, click a blank area to close the class plan details page.
Building on what we have learned, let's create a class plan with multi-week rotation.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.sdg.profileSettingsWindow.classPlans.isCurrentWeekFull"] == true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.profileEditing/reject.multiweek-classplans.full")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Now, click the New class plan button under the day you want (e.g. Monday) to create a class plan.
👉 In Time layout, pick a time layout, then enable multi-week rotation under Trigger rule, and click Create to make the class plan.
We now have a class plan with multi-week rotation. Please arrange its lessons to match your real schedule.
👉 Now, click the Next week button to switch to next week.
After switching to next week, you will notice the plan we just created is gone — it does not satisfy its activation rule this week, so it is not active.
👉 Now, click the New class plan button under the same day where you created the rotating plan.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.sdg.profileSettingsWindow.classPlans.isCurrentWeekFull"] == true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.profileEditing/reject.multiweek-classplans.full")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: As you can see, the new-plan screen has carried over what you entered for this day last week and set the rotation accordingly — you only need to change what should differ.
You can also tick Copy from to copy lessons from the original plan, so you only need to adjust the lessons that differ.
👉 Once everything is set, click Create to make the class plan.
🎉 Congratulations! You have successfully created a class plan with multi-week rotation.
Now, combining what you have learned, fill in the plan to match your real timetable.

Content.Title: This week's plans are full
Content.Content: It looks like this week's plans are full. Switch to another week with room left, then continue the tutorial.

Content.Title: No class plans this week
Content.Content: It looks like there are no class plans this week. Create one — or switch to a week that has plans — and then continue the tutorial.

Tutorials.Title: Component Editing: The Basics
Tutorials.Description: A first look at customizing what appears on the main window.

Content.Content: Welcome to edit mode. Next, let's see how to edit the components on the main window in edit mode.

Content.Title: Toolbar
Content.Content: This is the toolbar. Click the buttons here to access edit mode's features.

Content.Title: Main window
Content.Content: This is the main window. You can edit its components directly by selecting and dragging them.

Content.Title: Panning the view
Content.Content: Hold the middle mouse button and drag, or drag a blank area with your finger, to pan the view.

Content.Title: Zooming
Content.Content: Scroll the mouse wheel, or pinch a blank area with two fingers, to zoom the view.

Content.Title: Resetting the view
Content.Content: You can also click this button to restore the default view.

Content.Title: Done
Content.Content: When you are finished editing, click the Done button to exit edit mode.
Now that you know the basics of edit mode, let's add a component to the main window.
Next, let's see how to add components to the main window.
👉 Click the Add component button to open the component library.
This is the component library. Drag a component from here onto the spot on the main window where you want it, and it will be inserted there.
👉 Now, try dragging a component you would like onto the main window.
Besides dragging, you can also click the plus (+) after a component row to add a component.
👉 Now, click a blank area to collapse the component library.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.editMode.mainDrawer.getState"]() != 2) then
		service.TryStartNextSentence()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Click the plus (+) after a main window line.
👉 Pick a component in the library, then click Add at the bottom right to add it to that main window line.
🎉 Congratulations! You now know how to add components to the main window!
Some components (such as the schedule component) have their own settings, which you can tweak for further customization.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.hasComponentWithSettings"]() != true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.componentsEditing/reject.noComponents")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Now, click to select this component.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.editMode.selectedComponent.hasSettings"] == true) then
		service.TryStartNextSentence()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Click the gear icon to open the component's settings.
This is the component's settings page, where you can adjust its options.
Component settings are generally independent of each other, so you can add several copies of the same component with different settings.
👉 Now, try adjusting this component's settings and see what changes.
You can also click here to add a hiding rule so this component hides automatically under certain conditions.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.editMode.mainDrawer.getState"]() == 0) then
		service.TryStartNextSentence()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 🎉 Congratulations! You now know how to adjust component settings!
This is a container component — it can hold other components to achieve effects like carousels and grouping. Next, we will see how to edit the components inside a container.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.hasContainerComponent"]() != true) then
		service.JumpToParagraph("classfabric.getStarted.componentsEditing/reject.noComponents")
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Now, click to select this component.
Content.Script:
function onInitializing()
	if (context["classfabric.mainWindow.editMode.selectedComponent.isContainer"] == true) then
		service.TryStartNextSentence()
		return false
	end
	return true
end

Content.Content: 👉 Click the expand icon to show the container's child components.
Here are the container's child components. Just like components on a main window line, you can edit them by dragging.
👉 Now, try adding a component into the container the same way you added one to the main window earlier. When you are done, click Next step to continue.
🎉 Congratulations! You now know how to manage the components inside a container!
The main window is made up of main window lines. Next, let's see how to edit them.

Content.Title: Adding a main window line
Content.Content: 👉 Click the New main window line button to add one.
As you can see, the line we just created has appeared. You can now add components to it the same way as before.

Content.Title: Reordering main window lines
Content.Content: Drag the handle on the left to reorder main window lines.
With multiple lines, each main window line can show its own notifications.

Content.Title: Line notifications
Content.Content: Click this bell button to turn a main window line's notifications on or off.

Content.Title: Line settings
Content.Content: Click this gear button to expand the line settings, where you can adjust the line's hiding rules and appearance.

Content.Title: Main line
Content.Content: Click this button to make this the main line — notifications will show here first.

Content.Title: Deleting a main window line
Content.Content: Click this button to delete this main window line.
🎉 Congratulations! You now know how to manage main window lines!

Content.Title: No matching components found
Content.Content: The current main window has no components matching this tutorial's requirements, so this lesson cannot run for now.
